To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rIL-2 increases the expression of perforin mRNA in the blood of melanoma patients and this effect is correlated to that of granzyme B mRNA expression.
the frequency of cells expressing the perforins gene or the grancyme B gene in peripheral blood is significantly increased in patients with metastasizing melanoma who are treated with rIL-2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the mechanisms of action of rIL-2 in patients with metastasis of malignant melanoma.
the expression of the perforin and grazyme B genes in the peripheral blood cells of patients with melanoma treated with IL-2.
the study of the mechanisms of resistance of melanoma metastasis to immunotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of the granzymes and perforin genes in patients with malignancy treated with rIL-2 may be a marker of clinical response.
rIL-2 is an effective immunomodulating agent in patients with metastases from malignant melanoma, and that its effects on the cellular immune system are complex and not easily predictable.
perforin and/or granzyme B mRNA expression is not a reliable marker of clinical response in melanoma patients treated with rIL-2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

rIL-2 therapy increases the frequency of cytotoxic cells in peripheral blood of melanoma patients, and this increase is correlated with an increase in the expression of perforin, a cytotoxic effector molecule.
rIL-2 induced an activation of cytotoxic cells in the peripheral blood of patients suffering from metastasized melanoma.

the frequency of perforin and/or granzyme B positive cells in the peripheral blood of patients suffering from metastasized melanoma is significantly correlated with the expression of these genes in the primary melanoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the expression of the perforin and gransyme B genes can be induced by rIL- 2 in patients with metastases.
IL-2 treatment increases the expression of genes involved in the killing of target cells by cytotoxic cells.
IL-2 can increase the expression of the granzymes B and perforin genes, which are involved in the cytolytic activity of lymphocytes, in patients with metastases of melanoma.
